rows.honest_notes: the twist row: a $4 first year against a $25.04 renewal is churn-driven registration economics, exactly the cheap-year pattern interisle documents phishers exploiting (top 27 highest-abuse tlds priced at us$2 or less; 51% of abusive registrations in the new gtlds). the pattern holds across storefronts: porkbun runs the same cliff, $5.66 first year against $34.50 (2026-10-15). and the renewal is where they get you: a $4 .ltd registered two years ago has paid $25.04 twice, and each paid renewal weakens the sale-price prior, because keeping the domain now costs real money. registration age is per-domain evidence read at engine time (whois creation date), never a class verdict. price pressure raises a prior about economics; the abuse band stays unknown because the current datasets do not rank it, and a cheap promo alone proves nothing about abuse

rows.barrier_citation: usTLD Nexus Requirements (ntia.gov usTLD policy PDF): a registrant must be a us citizen, permanent resident, or a us business/organization with a us nexus; cloudflare's registrar docs confirm registrants identify their qualifying category. read 2026-10-15
rows.abuse_citation: not ranked in the interisle top tables read 2026-10-14: the tables are top-20 by count and rate and .us did not make the cut, which is a coverage statement, never a safety claim
rows.honest_notes: premierity: no sale price changes the barrier. a cheap .us promo still runs through an attested us nexus, so the human path here is shaped by eligibility, not economics. the honest nuance: the nexus is attested by the registrant at most registrars, an attestation is a raised cost of entry, not a document check; what each registrar actually verifies is a per-registrar fact for the registrar table

rows.barrier_citation: IEDR registration and naming policy (iedr.ie policy PDF): a documented claim of a real and substantive connection to ireland, with supporting documentation whose expiry must be in the future; the 2018 liberalisation removed the claim to the name but kept the documented connection claim. read 2026-10-15
rows.abuse_citation: not ranked in the interisle top tables read 2026-10-14 (coverage statement, never a safety claim)
rows.honest_notes: the barrier is a document-checked claim, stronger than an attestation: the registry checks the paperwork before the domain goes live. cheap .ie promos, where they exist, still require the claim, so price pressure alone cannot inflate registrations here the way it can on an open tld

rows.barrier_citation: DENIC verification for .de domains (denic.de: verification by letter or email from DENIC); germany implemented the EU NIS2 directive into national law effective 2025-12-06, imposing new holder verification requirements on registration and management of .de domains (IONOS help center, read 2026-10-15)
rows.abuse_citation: not ranked in the interisle top tables read 2026-10-14 (coverage statement, never a safety claim)
rows.honest_notes: the barrier is holder address verification under NIS2: the registry verifies the registrant, not just takes an attestation. the newest barrier in the registry (effective 2025-12-06) and the one most likely to keep changing; recheck the policy at every cadence tick
